done_when: Find which one it is: if Forge can return before the app-server process exits, make it wait for the exit; if it's only the check, make the test tell a leftover process from a reused PID. test_4_turn_log passes on Windows CI three runs in a row

findings.body: The new predicate still cannot distinguish a leftover shim from a reused PID when the replacement process is also cmd.exe. This is relevant to this suite: tests/conftest.py:50–52 creates .cmd shims for test commands, and .github/workflows/forge-next.yml:34 runs tests concurrently. An unrelated shim acquiring a reported PID therefore still fails the assertion after the original server has exited. Compare the original process's creation time and command, or retain its process handle, instead of treating the executable name as identity. This leaves the required PID-reuse distinction incomplete.

findings.body: Both uses of the new helper assert only that it returns false after normal cleanup. No test establishes that it detects a still-running shim or distinguishes a replacement process; replacing the Windows implementation with `return False` would satisfy every changed assertion. Add regression coverage exercising a live shim, its exit, and replacement identity (including another cmd.exe), with observable process behavior rather than only mocked tasklist output. The existing integration test does not independently validate the new check that is meant to resolve this flake.
findings.title: Not done: Test that the Windows process check detects a live server and rejects a reused PID

why: tests/test_codex_worker.py::test_4_turn_log fails on Windows CI about one run in two: right after forge work returns, tasklist still lists one of the four reported Codex app-server PIDs (either Forge returns before the process has fully exited on Windows, or Windows reused the PID)
